name: Tanchjim Bunny (USB version)
notes: V-shaped budget DD, dirt cheap. Vocals are actually amazing, best part of it by far. Bass is basically not there though — don't buy this expecting any rumble. Treble surprised me too, cleaner than Wan'er 2 honestly. Housing's big plastic and not that comfy, cable's cheap and smells bad. Only real reason to grab the USB version is the EQ app — genuinely powerful, worth it if you want to fix the bass yourself.
summary:
Sound Signature: Neutral
No dominant frequency colouration — relatively even response across the board.

⚠️ Weak areas: Bass.
🎵 Best for: General listening.

Verdict: Decent (5.2/10) — Gets the job done, some compromises.
Sound-only (excl. Value): 5.2/10
Pure Audio (excl. Fit & Value): 5.2/10

name: ZiiGaat Odyssey
notes: Bass is the best out of everything I've tried — hits hard and controlled. Treble's way smoother than I expected too, not harsh at all (other reviews online say pretty much the same, though they mention detail retrieval isn't its strongest point). Vocals are a bit weird in presentation but still good, mids otherwise natural. Shell feels solid but the stock cable is flimsy as hell, feels like it could snap. Isolation is stupid good — actually too good, gave me dizziness/pressure and made it hard to wear for long sessions. Funny thing is other reviews say isolation's just okay because of a vent by the connectors, so it's probably just my ears/fit. Cable and eartips are straight up bad for a $200 iem.
summary:
Sound Signature: Bass-heavy
Strong bass presence dominates — exciting for bass-driven genres but can overwhelm the midrange.

✅ Strong areas: Bass, Treble, Technical.
✅ Smooth, non-fatiguing treble — sibilance is well-controlled.
🎵 Best for: EDM, Hip-hop, Live rock, Classical, Jazz.
💰 Poor value — better alternatives likely exist at this price.

Verdict: Good (6.7/10) — Above average, enjoyable daily driver.

name: Cozoy D1
notes: Drier and less bassy than the Zii Rumba and Wan'er 2 — thinner low end but cleaner, tighter bass. Vocals/upper mids sit more forward and clear (checked squig.link FR vs Crinacle target, tracks close to the Zii through bass/mids but pulls ahead 2-4khz). Treble's more jagged, some peaks around 8-11khz give it a metallic, energetic edge instead of the smoother safer top end on the Rumba.

name: ZiiGaat x Vivir Digital Rumba
notes: Fun basshead-leaning tuning, sub-bass hits with decent control. Vocals pushed forward (some pinna gain around 2.5-3khz apparently), treble's smooth/safe but feels a bit closed-in on air. At $35 it's up against Truthear Gate (~$20, more neutral-warm, wider stage) and Wan'er 2 (~$20-25, more vocal-forward, better accessories) — both cheaper and already proven. Kiwi Ears Cadenza II ($49.99) is on my radar too but haven't re-tested it. Need to actually revisit this with a real listen before trusting these numbers.

name: Hidizs My Lin
notes: DD+BA hybrid collab. Pretty hard V-shape — bass is boosted a lot, mids are noticeably scooped so instruments sound a bit thin, and there's a sharp treble peak around 6-7khz that's the loudest part of the whole FR. That peak adds some perceived detail but also causes real sibilance. Air rolls off pretty steep after that. L/R channel matching felt spot on though. Build and comfort are above average for the price.

name: Tangzu Cai Wenji
notes: Cheap single DD. Warm-neutral, mids/vocals are the focus especially female vocals. Good for J-pop, acoustic, podcasts — natural and intimate. Bass is soft, no punch, bad for EDM/hip-hop. Detail and separation are just average. Soundstage's narrow so it feels a bit boxed in. Treble's smooth with barely any sibilance though, easy to listen to for hours.
